_comment: ALERT-STREAM op for a FULL-CADENCE survey night. Same product as op_2v_stream.json (the ~10k/night ranked QA stream), but the gates are tighter because the stream op is CADENCE-DEPENDENT -- a single fixed op does NOT give a comparable stream on every night.
_why: Measured on 20260629 (165 visits, 15,202 panels, 2.70M detections, 33 linkable pointing groups with ~42 min visit gaps) versus 20260630 (27 visits, 1,869 panels, 388k detections, ~4 groups with ~20 min gaps). Two effects compound: (1) ~8x more linkable groups, and (2) chance links scale as dt^2, so 42 min gaps give ~4.6x the chance-pair rate of 20 min gaps at equal density. Running op_2v_stream.json unchanged on 20260629 did not finish ONE pointing group in 42 minutes and extrapolated to several hundred thousand alerts.
_calibration: Pilot links on the largest pointing group (visits 2026062900777/2026062900829, 68,878 dets = 5% of the night's linkable detections), scaled to the night by the n^2-weighted group-size factor 14.5x:  chi2<=10 -> 331 alerts (2m50s) -> ~4,800/night;  chi2<=22 -> 899 (8m14s) -> ~13,000;  chi2<=18 interpolates to ~10,000. score_min 0.70 (not 0.50) is what makes it TRACTABLE: it cuts the pilot group from 68,878 to 9,155 linkable dets, and seeding cost goes as density^2. chi2 filters AFTER the orbit solve, so loosening it buys alerts at little runtime cost -- which is why the volume knob here is chi2, not score.  RETUNED for a ~20k-alert full-cadence target (user, 2026-07-28): chi2<=18 gave 6,811 alerts on the full 20260629 (the n^2-weighted pilot extrapolation predicted ~10k, i.e. it overestimated by ~1.5x, so trust the full-night number). chi2 is very nearly linear in yield here, so 30 targets ~11k; score_min 0.65 is the lever if more is needed, at ~4x the runtime since seeding goes as density^2.
_note: Volume is still finally set by rank: run_night renders the top --stream-top-n by calibrated P(real). This op only has to put the night in the right ballpark and, more importantly, keep the link tractable.
